examples: We danced a jig.
The band played a jig.
She did a happy jig.

more.def: A fast, lively folk dance from Ireland and Scotland, or the music for it.
examples: The fiddler played a jig, and everyone started dancing.
He did a little jig when he heard the good news.
An Irish jig has quick steps and bouncing jumps.

easy.def: To shake with small, quick moves.
examples: The jelly jiggled.
I jiggled the handle.
Her belly jiggled when she laughed.

more.def: To move with quick, small shakes up and down or side to side.
examples: The jelly jiggled on the plate when I tapped the table.
Dad jiggled the handle to make the toilet stop running.
The leaves jiggled in the wind.

easy.def: A puzzle made of many pieces that fit together.
examples: We did a jigsaw.
The jigsaw has a hundred pieces.
A jigsaw of a farm.

more.def: A puzzle made of many small, oddly shaped pieces that you fit together to make a picture; also a saw for cutting curves.
examples: We spread the jigsaw pieces out on the table and found the corners first.
The jigsaw showed a picture of a farm with a red barn.
Dad used a jigsaw to cut a curve in the wood.

easy.def: To make a light ringing sound.
examples: The bells jingle.
The keys jingled.
The sleigh bells jingled.

more.def: To make a light, ringing sound, as small bells do.
examples: The bells on the sleigh jingled.
The keys jingled in my pocket.
The coins jingled in her purse.
The jingle is catchy.
I sang the jingle.
The ad has a jingle.

more.def: A short, catchy tune or song that is used in an ad.
examples: The ad had a catchy jingle.
I sang the jingle all day.
The jingle for the cereal stuck in my head.
The jinx broke.
Do not mention the jinx.
A jinx on the team.

more.def: A person or thing that is thought to bring bad luck.
examples: The team thought it had a jinx.
Do not say that, or you will jinx it.
The jinx seemed to follow them.
